answer: A registry gives each verified agent a non-transferable reputation token earned only after a costly, checkable history of honest work, so fake identities cannot buy trust in bulk. Payments and access then weight that record, not raw account count. Like a haven in a rising tide, the system shelters genuine agents while cheap copies wash away, and the pigment of behaviour in every agent, its unique pattern of tasks, prices and replies, becomes a fingerprint that makes mass duplication visible and unprofitable.
